stack.name: Full Stack .NET Developer
stack.summary: A 12-week plan to pass senior full stack .NET interviews: modern C# and .NET 10, async and performance, ASP.NET Core, SQL and EF Core, security, architecture, distributed systems, cloud delivery, testing and observability, React with TypeScript, AI integration and system design.

weeks.goal: Answer language and platform questions at senior depth, and plan a move to .NET 10, since .NET 8 and 9 both leave support on 2026-11-10.
weeks.title: Modern C# and the .NET 10 platform

lessons.title: Types, memory layout and value semantics
topics: Value types vs reference types: layout, copying and where they live
Boxing, including hidden boxing through interfaces
Records and record structs: value equality and its pitfalls with mutable members
Nullable reference types: compile-time analysis, not runtime checks
lessons.exercise: Write three snippets that box without an obvious cast and one record whose equality surprises; explain each.

lessons.title: C# 12 to 14, and what comes in C# 15
topics: Primary constructors and collection expressions
Pattern matching: property, list and relational patterns; switch expressions
C# 14: field-backed properties, extension members and implicit span conversions
C# 15 preview: unions and closed hierarchies
lessons.exercise: Refactor a class hierarchy with type checks into switch expressions, then rewrite a helper class as C# 14 extension members.

lessons.title: Generics, LINQ internals and source generators
topics: Generic constraints, covariance and contravariance
Deferred vs immediate execution; multiple enumeration
`IEnumerable<T>` vs `IQueryable<T>`, expression trees and query providers
Source generators: what they replace (reflection) and when to use them
lessons.exercise: Implement a custom LINQ operator with `yield return`, then show where multiple enumeration causes duplicate work.

lessons.title: The .NET release model and migrating to .NET 10
topics: LTS vs STS, support dates, and why .NET 8 ending in November 2026 matters
Porting from .NET Framework: assessment, incremental migration, removed APIs such as `BinaryFormatter`
Moving .NET 8 to .NET 10: breaking changes and testing
Native AOT and trimming: startup and size gains, and reflection limits
lessons.exercise: Assess a sample project for .NET 10: list blocking APIs, packages and the migration order.

milestones.title: Refresh your CV and LinkedIn for senior .NET roles: lead with scale, ownership and measurable impact

weeks.deliverable: A short migration plan for a real or sample .NET Framework or .NET 8 app to .NET 10, plus a C# kata that uses records, pattern matching and C# 14 features.
interview_checks: Why can a record with a `List<T>` property break value equality?
What is the difference between `IEnumerable<T>` and `IQueryable<T>` when you add a `Where`?
How would you migrate a .NET Framework 4.8 app to .NET 10, and what would you do first?
What does Native AOT give you, and what does it cost?

weeks.goal: Explain async and the garbage collector at the level of internals, and diagnose production performance problems with measurements instead of guesses.
weeks.title: Async, concurrency, GC and performance

lessons.title: How async/await works
topics: The compiler-generated state machine and continuations
`Task`, `ValueTask` and `IAsyncEnumerable<T>`
Sync-over-async deadlocks, `SynchronizationContext` and `ConfigureAwait`
`async void`, cancellation with `CancellationToken`, and exceptions from `Task.WhenAll`
lessons.exercise: Reproduce a sync-over-async deadlock in a UI app, explain it, and show why the same code does not deadlock in ASP.NET Core.

lessons.title: Threads, the thread pool and synchronization
topics: How the thread pool grows, and what starvation looks like
`lock`, `SemaphoreSlim`, `Interlocked` and when each fits
Concurrent collections and the `GetOrAdd` factory gotcha
Channels and `Parallel.ForEachAsync` for bounded concurrency
lessons.exercise: Call a downstream API 1,000 times with at most 10 calls in flight, first with `SemaphoreSlim` and then with `Parallel.ForEachAsync`.

lessons.title: The garbage collector and memory
topics: Generations, the Large Object Heap and the Pinned Object Heap
Workstation, Server and DATAS modes
`IDisposable`, finalizers and common leak sources
`Span<T>`, `Memory<T>` and `ArrayPool<T>` for allocation-free code
lessons.exercise: Rewrite a string-splitting parser with `ReadOnlySpan<char>` and measure allocations with BenchmarkDotNet.

lessons.title: Performance diagnostics lab
topics: Tool escalation: dotnet-counters, dotnet-stack, dotnet-trace, dotnet-dump
Reading p50 vs p99 latency and RED/USE dashboards
Proving a change with BenchmarkDotNet
What changed for performance in .NET 10
lessons.exercise: Find a planted memory leak from a heap dump and a planted starvation from counters, and write a two-paragraph postmortem for each.

milestones.title: Build: start a portfolio API (ASP.NET Core, EF Core, React client) that you will grow each week

weeks.deliverable: A diagnostics write-up: a planted thread-pool starvation and a memory leak, each found with dotnet-counters, dotnet-trace or dotnet-dump, and fixed.
interview_checks: What does `await` compile to, and what does `ConfigureAwait(false)` change?
Why can `ConcurrentDictionary.GetOrAdd` run your factory twice?
CPU is at 20% but requests are timing out. What do you check?
What are GC generations and the Large Object Heap, and how do they affect latency?

weeks.goal: Know the request pipeline end to end and design APIs other teams can depend on: DI, middleware, contracts, caching and rate limiting.
weeks.title: ASP.NET Core internals and API design

lessons.title: The host, middleware and routing
topics: The generic host, `WebApplication` and Kestrel
Middleware order and short-circuiting; middleware vs filters
Endpoint routing and route constraints
Minimal APIs vs controllers: features and trade-offs
lessons.exercise: Write a correlation-id and timing middleware, place it correctly in the pipeline, and test the order.

lessons.title: Dependency injection and configuration
topics: Singleton, scoped and transient lifetimes; scope validation
Captive dependencies and `IServiceScopeFactory`
Keyed services, factories and decorators
Configuration providers, the options pattern and `ValidateOnStart`
lessons.exercise: Inject a scoped service into a singleton, show the startup error, and fix it two ways.

lessons.title: API contracts
topics: REST resources, status codes and ProblemDetails
Versioning, pagination and idempotency keys
OpenAPI 3.1 in ASP.NET Core 10 and validation
gRPC and SignalR: when REST is the wrong fit
lessons.exercise: Design an orders API with idempotent creation, cursor pagination and optimistic concurrency, and publish its OpenAPI document.

lessons.title: Caching, rate limiting and background work
topics: Output caching vs response caching
HybridCache: L1 and L2, stampede protection and tag invalidation
Rate limiting: fixed window, sliding window, token bucket and concurrency limiters
`BackgroundService` and graceful shutdown
lessons.exercise: Put HybridCache in front of a slow query, simulate a stampede, and show only one call reaches the database.

milestones.title: Apply to five senior .NET roles (LinkedIn, Bdjobs, remote boards), each with a tailored summary

weeks.deliverable: Your portfolio API with custom middleware, validated options, ProblemDetails errors, OpenAPI 3.1, HybridCache and rate limiting.
interview_checks: What is a captive dependency, and how does ASP.NET Core catch it?
Middleware or a filter: how do you choose?
How do you make a POST endpoint idempotent?
What does HybridCache's stampede protection do, and what does its invalidation not do?

weeks.goal: Read and tune the SQL behind your code, use EF Core without surprises, and change schemas without downtime.
weeks.title: Data: SQL and EF Core

lessons.title: SQL performance and transactions
topics: Clustered, non-clustered, covering and filtered indexes
Reading execution plans: seeks, scans and key lookups
Isolation levels, locking, row versioning and deadlocks
SQL Server and PostgreSQL differences that matter to .NET developers
lessons.exercise: Capture the plan for a slow query, add one index to remove a key lookup, and record the change.

lessons.title: EF Core queries
topics: The change tracker, tracking vs no-tracking queries and projections
N+1 queries, eager loading, split queries and cartesian explosion
Client vs server evaluation, global query filters and compiled queries
Raw SQL and Dapper: when to leave LINQ
lessons.exercise: Fix an endpoint with an N+1 two ways (Include and projection) and compare round trips.

lessons.title: EF Core writes and migrations
topics: Optimistic concurrency with row versions
Transactions and `SaveChanges` atomicity
Bulk `ExecuteUpdate` and `ExecuteDelete`
Migrations in production: scripts, bundles and expand/contract changes
lessons.exercise: Plan a zero-downtime column rename as a series of deployable migrations.

lessons.title: Scaling data
topics: Read replicas and read-your-own-writes
Caching layers and their consistency
Multi-tenancy: database, schema or row-level isolation
When to use a document or key-value store instead
lessons.exercise: Choose a multi-tenancy model for a SaaS product and defend it in a one-page note.

milestones.title: Practice: answer three SQL tuning questions aloud and record yourself

weeks.deliverable: An EF Core data layer with no N+1 queries, optimistic concurrency and a zero-downtime migration plan, plus before-and-after execution plans for two slow queries.
interview_checks: What is the N+1 problem, and how do you find it with EF Core?
Clustered, non-clustered and covering indexes: explain each.
Which isolation level would you use for a balance transfer, and why?
How do you rename a column with zero downtime?

weeks.goal: Secure a full stack .NET app end to end: OAuth 2.0 and OIDC flows, authorization, the OWASP Top 10 and secret handling.
weeks.title: Identity and application security

lessons.title: OAuth 2.0, OIDC and tokens
topics: Authorization code with PKCE, and client credentials for services
ID tokens vs access tokens; validating a JWT
Cookies vs tokens in SPAs and the BFF pattern
Refresh tokens, rotation and revocation
lessons.exercise: Secure an API with JWT bearer auth and list every validation parameter you set and why.

lessons.title: Authentication and authorization in ASP.NET Core
topics: Authentication schemes and handlers
Policies, requirements and resource-based authorization
Microsoft Entra ID for apps and APIs
Passkeys in ASP.NET Core 10
lessons.exercise: Allow editing a document only by its owner or an admin with a resource-based authorization handler.

lessons.title: OWASP Top 10 in .NET
topics: Injection and parameterized queries in EF Core and Dapper
XSS, CSRF, antiforgery tokens and SameSite cookies
SSRF and insecure deserialization
Secrets, Key Vault and managed identities
lessons.exercise: Audit a sample app against the OWASP Top 10 and fix the three worst findings.

lessons.title: Security in the delivery pipeline
topics: Static and dynamic analysis (SAST and DAST)
Dependency and container scanning
Threat modelling with STRIDE
Handling a vulnerability disclosure
lessons.exercise: Threat-model your portfolio app and add dependency scanning to its CI.

milestones.title: Build: add login, roles and a security section to your portfolio README

weeks.deliverable: Your API protected with OIDC and JWT bearer tokens, a BFF for the React client, resource-based authorization and a short threat model.
interview_checks: Walk through the authorization code flow with PKCE.
Cookies or tokens for a SPA calling your API? Justify it.
How does ASP.NET Core protect against CSRF, and when do you need it?
Where do secrets live in development, CI and production?

weeks.goal: Structure large codebases so they stay changeable, and argue the trade-offs of each style rather than following one by habit.
weeks.title: Architecture: modular monolith, DDD and CQRS

lessons.title: Architecture styles
topics: Layered, clean/onion and vertical slice architectures
The modular monolith and enforcing module boundaries
Where validation, transactions and logging belong
Recognizing over-engineering
lessons.exercise: Implement one feature as a vertical slice and compare it with the same feature in a layered design.

lessons.title: Domain-driven design
topics: Entities, value objects and aggregates
Invariants and domain events
Bounded contexts and context maps
Anemic vs rich domain models
lessons.exercise: Model an order aggregate that enforces its invariants, with value objects for money and address.

lessons.title: CQRS and event sourcing
topics: Separate read and write models without separate databases
Mediator pipelines and the MediatR licensing question
Event sourcing: what it gives you and when not to use it
Read models and projections
lessons.exercise: Add a read model to one feature and write down what the added complexity bought you.

lessons.title: Architecture review
topics: Inheriting a codebase with competing patterns
Prioritizing technical debt
Writing architecture decision records
Presenting a review to the team
lessons.exercise: Review the eShop reference app and present three decisions you agree with and one you would change.

milestones.title: Apply to five more roles and ask two people in your network for referrals

weeks.deliverable: Three ADRs for your portfolio app covering its architecture style, module boundaries and whether it uses CQRS.
interview_checks: Clean architecture, vertical slices or a modular monolith: how do you choose?
What is an aggregate, and how do you pick its boundary?
When is CQRS worth its complexity, and would you still use MediatR now that it is commercially licensed?
When would you not use event sourcing?

weeks.goal: Build reliable distributed .NET systems: when to split services, messaging semantics, the outbox, idempotency and resilience.
weeks.title: Distributed systems and messaging

lessons.title: Microservices decisions
topics: Monolith vs microservices: team size, deployability and data ownership
Synchronous vs asynchronous communication
API gateways and YARP
The strangler fig pattern for migrations
lessons.exercise: Write an ADR arguing for or against splitting one module of your app into a service.

lessons.title: Message brokers
topics: Queues and topics; Azure Service Bus, RabbitMQ and Kafka compared
Delivery guarantees, ordering and partitions
Dead-letter queues and poison messages
Choosing a broker for a workload
lessons.exercise: Publish an event from one service and consume it in another with a dead-letter policy.

lessons.title: Consistency: outbox, idempotency and sagas
topics: The dual-write problem and the transactional outbox and inbox
Idempotency keys and idempotent consumers
Sagas: orchestration vs choreography and compensation
Explaining eventual consistency to product owners
lessons.exercise: Add an outbox so a crash between saving and publishing loses nothing, and prove it with a test.

lessons.title: Resilience and local orchestration
topics: Timeouts, retries with jitter, circuit breakers and hedging
The .NET resilience libraries and Polly
`IHttpClientFactory` and socket exhaustion
Aspire for running and wiring services locally
lessons.exercise: Wrap a flaky downstream call with the standard resilience handler and show its behavior under injected faults.

milestones.title: Practice: one mock system design interview with a peer

weeks.deliverable: Two services that talk through a broker with an outbox, idempotent consumers and resilient HTTP calls, run locally with Aspire.
interview_checks: How does the transactional outbox solve the dual-write problem?
What does at-least-once delivery force your consumers to do?
How do you stop one slow dependency from taking down every service?
When is a monolith the right answer?

weeks.goal: Ship .NET apps to the cloud: Azure hosting choices with their AWS equivalents, containers, Kubernetes basics, CI/CD and infrastructure as code.
weeks.title: Cloud and delivery

lessons.title: Azure hosting, with AWS equivalents
topics: App Service, Container Apps, AKS and Functions
The AWS equivalents: Elastic Beanstalk, ECS/Fargate, EKS and Lambda
Managed identities and networking basics
Cost and scaling trade-offs
lessons.exercise: Pick a hosting option for three different workloads and justify each on cost and operations.

lessons.title: Containers and Kubernetes
topics: Multi-stage Dockerfiles and `dotnet publish` container support
Chiseled images, non-root users and image size
Kubernetes basics: probes, configuration, scaling
How the GC behaves under container memory limits
lessons.exercise: Containerize the API, run it as non-root, and compare image sizes across base images.

lessons.title: CI/CD and infrastructure as code
topics: Build once, deploy many: artifacts and environments
Blue/green, canary and rolling deployments; feature flags
Bicep vs Terraform
Database changes in the pipeline
lessons.exercise: Build a pipeline that tests, scans and deploys to staging, with a manual gate before production.

lessons.title: Deploying with Aspire
topics: Aspire app model and service defaults
Deploying to Container Apps or Kubernetes
Configuration and secrets across environments
Scalability and cost reviews
lessons.exercise: Deploy your two-service system with Aspire and document how it scales.

milestones.title: Apply to five more roles and follow up on earlier applications

weeks.deliverable: Your app containerized and deployed to Azure Container Apps from GitHub Actions, with infrastructure defined as code.
interview_checks: App Service, Container Apps, AKS or Functions: how do you choose, and what are the AWS equivalents?
How do you make a .NET container image small and safe?
Blue/green or canary: trade-offs?
How do you roll back a release that included a database migration?

weeks.goal: Design a test strategy that catches regressions cheaply, and instrument services so production problems can be found from telemetry.
weeks.title: Testing and observability

lessons.title: Unit testing and test design
topics: xUnit facts, theories and fixtures
Mocks, stubs and fakes; the cost of over-mocking
Testing behavior, not implementation
Testing time and async code with `TimeProvider`
lessons.exercise: Rewrite a brittle mock-heavy test into a behavior-focused test with a fake.

lessons.title: Integration and contract tests
topics: `WebApplicationFactory` and replacing services
Testcontainers for SQL Server, PostgreSQL and brokers
Database reset strategies
Contract tests between services
lessons.exercise: Write an integration test that runs the API against a database container and checks a full request.

lessons.title: Observability with OpenTelemetry
topics: Logs, metrics and traces; structured logging
`ActivitySource`, `Meter` and context propagation
Exporting to Application Insights or Grafana
SLIs, SLOs and alerting on symptoms
lessons.exercise: Instrument both services and view one trace that spans HTTP and the message broker.

lessons.title: Incident drill
topics: Finding a p99 regression from traces and metrics
Spotting thread-pool starvation from counters
Running an incident: roles, communication, rollback
Blameless postmortems
lessons.exercise: Run a drill on a planted regression and write the postmortem.

milestones.title: Build: CI runs unit and integration tests on every pull request

weeks.deliverable: Unit and integration tests (WebApplicationFactory and Testcontainers) in CI, and OpenTelemetry traces and metrics across both services.
interview_checks: What makes a unit test brittle?
Why run integration tests against a real database in a container?
How do you trace one request across three services?
p99 latency doubled after a release. How do you find out why?

weeks.goal: Be credible on the front end: React is in 67% of senior .NET postings, so learn TypeScript and React's rendering model well, with one lesson for Angular shops.
weeks.title: React and TypeScript for .NET engineers

lessons.title: TypeScript for C# developers
topics: Structural typing, unions, intersections and narrowing
Generics, `keyof`, mapped and conditional types
`unknown` vs `any` and exhaustiveness with `never`
Generating API types from OpenAPI
lessons.exercise: Model an API result as a discriminated union and write an exhaustive render function.

lessons.title: React's rendering model
topics: Render and commit; reconciliation and keys
Hooks, effects and stale closures
Context and its re-render cost
`useTransition`, `useDeferredValue` and the React Compiler
lessons.exercise: Fix a stale-closure bug in an interval hook and an unnecessary re-render in a list.

lessons.title: Data, state and testing on the front end
topics: Server state vs client state; TanStack Query caching and invalidation
Forms, validation and optimistic updates
Auth with a BFF
Testing Library, Playwright and accessibility (WCAG)
lessons.exercise: Replace effect-based fetching with TanStack Query, add an optimistic update, and cover the flow with a Playwright test.

lessons.title: Angular for Angular shops, and where Blazor fits
topics: Angular signals, zoneless change detection and OnPush
RxJS flattening operators: `switchMap` vs `exhaustMap`
Lazy routes and bundle size
Blazor render modes and when a .NET-only team picks it
lessons.exercise: Build the same list page in Angular with signals and compare it with the React version.

milestones.title: Build: publish your full stack portfolio app with a README explaining its design decisions

weeks.deliverable: A React and TypeScript client for your API with generated API types, server-state caching, a BFF login, and Playwright tests.
interview_checks: What triggers a React re-render, and how do you avoid unnecessary ones?
Why do index keys break lists?
What does TanStack Query do that `useEffect` plus `fetch` does not?
Signals or RxJS in Angular: when do you use each?

weeks.goal: Build LLM features in .NET and review AI-written code responsibly, since about half of senior postings now ask for one or the other.
weeks.title: AI and LLM integration in .NET

lessons.title: LLMs for engineers and Microsoft.Extensions.AI
topics: Tokens, context windows, cost and latency
Failure modes: hallucination, prompt injection, non-determinism
`IChatClient`, streaming and structured output
Caching, retries and rate limits for model calls
lessons.exercise: Add a streaming chat endpoint behind `IChatClient` and log tokens and cost per request.

lessons.title: Retrieval-augmented generation
topics: Embeddings and vector search (EF Core 10 on Azure SQL, pgvector)
Chunking and retrieval strategies
Grounding answers and citing sources
Evaluating retrieval and answer quality
lessons.exercise: Index your app's documents, answer questions with citations, and measure retrieval quality on 20 test questions.

lessons.title: Agents, tools and MCP
topics: Function calling and tool design
Microsoft Agent Framework
MCP servers and clients
Guardrails, permissions and human approval
lessons.exercise: Expose one read-only tool from your API to an agent and add an approval step for anything that writes.

lessons.title: Governing AI-assisted engineering
topics: Reviewing AI-generated code: correctness, security and licensing
Testing AI features
Data privacy and what may be sent to a model
Team policies for AI coding tools
lessons.exercise: Write a one-page team policy for AI coding tools and review an AI-generated pull request against it.

milestones.title: Apply to five more roles and prepare questions to ask each company

weeks.deliverable: A streaming chat feature in your app using Microsoft.Extensions.AI, with retrieval over your own data and one tool exposed to the model.
interview_checks: What drives the cost and latency of an LLM call, and how do you control them?
Walk through a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline and how you would evaluate it.
What is MCP, and how would you expose your API's data to an agent safely?
How do you review and test code written by an AI assistant?

weeks.goal: Pass the senior loop: system design with capacity math, leadership and behavioral stories, a short algorithms refresher, and a full mock.
weeks.title: System design, leadership and mock interviews

lessons.title: System design method
topics: Requirements, estimates, API, data model, high-level design and deep dives
A rate limiter and a notification system
Trade-off language: consistency, latency, cost and complexity
Designing with .NET and Azure building blocks
lessons.exercise: Design a notification system in 45 minutes and review it against the method.

lessons.title: A second design with capacity math
topics: Back-of-the-envelope estimation
A multi-tenant SaaS or chat system
Partitioning, replication and caching tiers
Handling failure and graceful degradation
lessons.exercise: Design a multi-tenant order pipeline with capacity estimates and a failure analysis.

lessons.title: Leadership stories and an algorithms refresher
topics: STAR stories: incidents, disagreement, mentoring and tech debt
Senior signals: scope, ambiguity and influence
Hash maps, trees, graphs and an LRU cache
What Bangladesh service companies and big-tech loops each test
lessons.exercise: Write five STAR stories and solve three medium problems under a timer.

lessons.title: Full mock loop
topics: A 45-minute .NET deep dive
A 45-minute system design
A 30-minute behavioral round
Turning feedback into a final study plan
lessons.exercise: Run the full mock loop with a peer and fix your weakest answer.

milestones.title: Run two full mock interviews and send follow-ups on every open application

weeks.deliverable: Two rehearsed system designs, five STAR stories and one full mock interview loop with notes on what to improve.
interview_checks: Design a rate limiter, then scale it across regions.
Design a multi-tenant SaaS order pipeline.
Tell me about a production incident you led. What changed afterwards?
How do you mentor a developer who is struggling?
